findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission adds resource name where group IDs are expected by callers
findings.body: In V2 the resource for a group is looked up by ID (hasPermission(groupId,...) calls resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)), so resources are named by group id; this is consistent. However the V2 loop over findByType adds groupResource.getId() (the internal resource UUID) to the granted set, not the group ID/name. Callers (UsersResource, BruteForceUsersResource, getUsersCount) pass this set to session.users() as group IDs, so the filter compares the wrong identifiers and group-based user visibility silently returns nothing for V2.

findings.title: policyStore.findByResource called on possibly null resource
findings.body: When the all-groups resource type resource is not found, getResourceTypeResource can return null, and the code then calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, causing an NPE. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (line 111). Null must be checked before the store lookup.

findings.title: canViewMembers in V2 ignores the global view/manage permission and group-specific scopes inconsistently
findings.body: canViewMembers returns true only for users().canView(), then checks VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the group. canManageMembers similarly. But canManageMembership in V2 checks only MANAGE_USERS role and not users().canManage(), so an admin with manage-users permission via FGAP is denied membership management while canManageMembers passes; this breaks the documented contract in GroupPermissionEvaluator that canManageMembership is true for MANAGE on the group.

findings.title: canView/canManage(null) evaluation grants via VIEW/MANAGE on all-groups resource only without checking ownership
findings.body: canView() and canManage() call hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) which, when resource is missing, falls back to the all-groups resource type. Any policy attached to the all-groups resource with VIEW or MANAGE is treated as a global group permission, so a single-group permission can be interpreted as global list/manage rights through the fallback path when evaluated via groupId null.

findings.title: isImpersonatable Javadoc/annotation placement leaves grantIfNoPermission undocumented and deprecation misplaced
findings.body: The @Deprecated annotation was moved onto isImpersonatable while the Javadoc for it was removed, and grantIfNoPermission lost its blank-line separation. The interface now has an undocumented deprecated method immediately followed by an unrelated method, reducing clarity of the API contract.

findings.title: Group listing no longer lets users with view-only global access see all groups
findings.body: The previous code computed canView() once and short-circuited the per-group check. The new code calls groupsEvaluator::canView per element, which for V2 performs a permission evaluation per group (performance regression) and, combined with the now-empty set semantics, can filter out groups a caller with global view should see if canView(group) does not short-circuit on global roles consistently.

findings.title: Permission resource ID check drops scope grants from all-users permissions
findings.body: hasPermission now requires permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). When evaluated against the all-users resource type resource, permissions returned are associated with that resource, but for user-specific resources the matching resource may be a different one; additionally getResourceId may be null for some permission types, causing NPE. The added check changes semantics without test coverage.

findings.title: Stray double semicolon and unused topGroup initialisation style issue in test
findings.body: The field declaration ends with ';;' and the test class sets a group name field that duplicates the group creation; minor, but indicates the test was not reviewed carefully. Also testManageGroupMembership contains a dangling blank line with trailing whitespace.
